A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Large Continual Instruction Assistant. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison through text extraction and rendered pages. Corresponding methods, experiments, equations, and displays can be matched, including Algorithm 1 moving from Appendix P to Q.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-tuning experiments, component ablations, robustness evaluations, and generated dialogue examples, including Tables 1–8 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains original LLaVA, Qwen-VL, and T5/InstrDialog results, together with ablations, robustness evaluations, and dialogue examples.

M1.justification: The applied dynamic EMA update, layerwise approximations, TF-IDF instruction grouping, and LoRA/Adapter procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E and Algorithm 1 retain the same implementation formula and steps. The formal objective revision is not propagated into a different applied procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight multimodal datasets, 19-task InstrDialog stream, and dialogue examples. Task-order and instruction-template coverage is retained. TRACE is added only to related work, without evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains identical within the corresponding experiments in Tables 1–3 and 6–8 and the qualitative comparisons. Added or repaired citations do not introduce newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix L, Eq. (50), reverses forgetting from final accuracy minus the earlier maximum to the earlier maximum minus final accuracy. This corrects the documented metric definition; the reported scores and other experimental settings remain unchanged, without evidence of reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix I and Table 10 remove the diagnostic evaluation of testing-stage instruction-matching accuracy. Group assignments remain, as do component ablations, fixed-EMA sensitivity results, task-order and instruction-template robustness tests, and qualitative case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations in Table 8 and retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice elsewhere. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Table 10 loses all 13 group-matching accuracy values, ranging from 96.79 to 99.76, and Appendix I drops the corresponding above-96% finding. Tables 1–8 retain their numerical results; for example, Table 1 still reports 64.64 Avg.ACC, 1.93 Forgetting, and 66.33 New.ACC for the proposed method.

T1.justification: New Appendix P, Eqs. (55)–(60), extends the existing scalar EMA derivation to high-dimensional parameters using a Hessian quadratic form. Eq. (7) gains an absolute value, and Eq. (50) corrects the forgetting definition. These are localized formal revisions; the existing scalar derivations and implemented approximation remain.

C1.justification: The central claims of reduced forgetting through dynamic EMA, limited parameter expansion through instruction grouping, and broad applicability remain. The abstract loses its numerical forgetting example, but that result and its interpretation remain in Table 1 and Section 5.2.

C2.justification: New Section 7 connects the method to lifelong assistants and argues that avoiding data rehearsal reduces privacy risks. Existing interpretations of robustness, knowledge retention, and hallucinations remain, as does the conclusion's limitation to image/text settings under computational constraints.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future code release with a concrete repository link and a statement of availability. Conversely, Section 5.1 and Appendix J remove the eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs and 80GB memory disclosure. Other implementation details remain; repository contents were not externally checked.

R1.justification: v4 adds a brief TRACE discussion and supporting citations, including Qwen-VL, TF-IDF, and T5, while removing several bibliography entries. These changes improve or adjust attribution without substantially redefining the paper's positioning relative to prior continual instruction tuning research.

P1.justification: There are scattered grammar and terminology edits, clarified LoRA baseline naming, updated author affiliations and correspondence information, and shortened appendix explanations. A short Impact Statement and new Appendix P are inserted, with Algorithm 1 relabeled under Appendix Q; the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 are retained. Tables 6 and 8 are typeset more compactly, Table 6 receives a more descriptive caption, and Table 10 loses its accuracy rows. Accompanying page reflow is limited rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the forgetting definition, repairs missing citations, and supplies a concrete code pointer. These benefits coexist with removal of Table 10's matching-accuracy validation and the hardware disclosure. The theoretical additions do not clearly resolve rigor concerns: Eq. (7) gains an absolute value that the unchanged Lagrangian in Eq. (8) does not incorporate. These opposing effects prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
